rubrics.justification: Describes an expanded blastocyst with visible ICM, adequate TE, and thinned zona consistent with the reported 3AA. Notes uncertainty from a static image. Minor overinterpretation in suggesting the image may look slightly less than textbook AA.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, endometrial thickness, BMI, first-cycle status, and sperm parameters well, and appropriately highlights hydrosalpinx as a key modifier of prognosis in tubal-factor IVF.

Overall logic is clear and conclusions are mostly supported. Probability estimate is reasonable, though there is some mild inconsistency between implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth framing and some hedging around morphology/euploidy.

Generally consistent with Gardner grading principles and standard IVF practice: favors single good-quality Day 5 transfer, emphasizes luteal support, uterine/tubal evaluation, and selective rather than routine PGT-A at age 33. Minor deviations include some speculative comments and nonstandard phrasing.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including confirming hydrosalpinx status, uterine cavity assessment, luteal support adherence, and selective future testing. Useful and case-specific, though some recommendations remain somewhat general.
